blocks.body:
# Hypervector v44 and $5,000 Portfolio Expansion Review

**Decision snapshot — 2026-08-12 00:31 EDT.** v39 remains a healthy live evidence collector with three protected open positions. v44 is the correct next canary topology, but it is a three-asset research portfolio—not yet a ten-position strategy and not yet evidence for scaling capital to $5,000.

## Decision

**Proceed to v44 only after v39 is flat and order-free, then run v44 at the current approximately $500 bankroll. Do not fund $5,000 yet.** The code, route contract, friction model, and transition tests are coherent. The missing evidence is repeatable forward profitability: v44 has no compatible closed-lifecycle window, its BTC specialists are sparse, and HYPE/SP500 remain forward research.

This is a measured progression, not capital-preservation mode: v44 allocates up to 23.20% margin and 1.16× gross account exposure when all three assets are open. The restraint is in refusing to invent seven extra positions from failed or technically unresolved candidates.

## What v39 taught us

The current run produced seven closed lifecycles: 1 win, 6 losses, −$2.392536 net, PF 0.0071. Fees consumed 476% of positive gross market PnL because the only winner was $0.017061. This is strong evidence that the represented route set should not be scaled as configured.

The loss was distributed across SNDK pressure, SPCX pressure, Hulk BTC, and onset BTC/ETH/SOL; ETH onset alone lost twice. **v44 removes every one of these six provider-symbol mappings.** That is the principal strategy fix. The three current open positions—ETH onset long, SOL onset short, and SP500 pressure short—remain protected by venue stops; their eventual outcomes are not included in the closed chart.

## What v44 changes

The successor reduces the live roster to BTC, HYPE, and SP500. BTC receives separate long and short specialists, but the one-position-per-asset rule makes those routes mutually exclusive. HYPE uses compression-pullback rather than the failed onset transfer. SP500 retains pressure breakout as an exact forward research route.

Every route has a venue stop and a time-based terminal fallback. BTC has explicit price targets; HYPE and SP500 primarily exit on strategy/opposite-signal handling or their time ceiling. The $51.38 p99 stop-wave estimate stacks small-sample live fee, depth, slippage, and funding components. It can be exceeded by gaps, outages, correlation, or stop slippage, so it is a sizing diagnostic—not a maximum-loss guarantee.

## Regime detector disposition

Canonical regime telemetry is populated and causal in the sampled v39 core routes, but its pooled primary direction classification is not a reliable universal entry gate in this prefix.

At 5–30 minutes, pooled TREND_UP and TREND_DOWN accuracy clusters around chance. TREND_UP reaches 61.4% at 60 minutes, while TREND_DOWN falls to 47.2%. Episode-onset TREND_DOWN is more encouraging at 66.7%/58.3%/50.0%/83.3% across 5/30/15/60 minutes, but only 12 onsets exist. Therefore v44 keeps regime as telemetry, conflict attribution, and conditional hold context. Promoting it to a hard entry gate would require a longer forward window with non-overlapping episode evidence.

## Candidate expansion evidence

MU, SKHX, and CL produced positive development economics under venue-matched nominal/stress replay. None is live-ready because most selected lifecycles cross incomplete mark-risk paths, and validation/holdout remained unopened.

SKHX is the strongest next technical challenger: stress PF 2.09 and +$12.91 on 34 development trades, positive after removing its largest winner, but 24/34 paths are unresolved. MU has 43/56 unresolved; its prospective pressure/candle parity is now encouraging but cannot repair historical risk-path evidence. CL has 59/81 unresolved and turns negative after removing the largest stress winner. MU, SKHX, and SNDK are also a correlated semiconductor cluster, so qualifying all three would not create three independent portfolio slots.

## Scope and methodology

The live section is bounded to checkpoint `bidirectional-live-1786453934555` through 2026-08-12T04:31:23Z. Closed PnL is authoritative venue lifecycle accounting after fees and funding. v44 risk uses its exact profile fingerprint and the $5,000 scenario from the route-aware friction artifact. Regime statistics use completed canonical bars from four symbols; observations overlap and are descriptive. MU/SKHX/CL comparisons use development-only $500 portfolio replays with nominal and stressed friction. Validation/holdout are explicitly not treated as evaluated when the technical path gate failed.

## Uncertainties and falsifiers

**High confidence** in the v39 accounting, v44 configuration topology, and deterministic sizing arithmetic because current checkpoints, immutable artifacts, and focused tests reconcile. **Medium confidence** that v44 is safer and more informative than v39 because all demonstrated v39 loser mappings are removed, but the replacement routes remain sparse. **Low confidence** in stable profitability until v44 accumulates compatible closes.

Update or reject this recommendation if: a fresh preflight changes venue fees/leverage materially; any v44 route lacks a stop or action/non-action accounting; v44 closes show PF below 1 after a meaningful sample; realized stop-wave loss materially exceeds the model; regime episode accuracy decays with more independent onsets; or any candidate resolves its technical paths and then fails untouched validation.

## Next actions

1. Keep v39 running until SOL and SP500 are flat and all owned orders are gone; do not hot-swap an open lifecycle.
2. Generate a fresh v44 preflight, verify exact profile fingerprint, three assets, four routes, six directional scopes, venue leverage, stops, fees, and zero blockers.
3. Activate v44 only with the already-required explicit live-risk flags, still at the approximately $500 bankroll.
4. Review every v44 close and every eligible-but-not-routed event; compare realized fee/slippage/funding with the stress artifact.
5. Finish SKHX prospective warmup/parity, then repair or replace missing exact mark-path evidence before opening untouched validation. Keep MU report-only and CL out of the roster.
6. Search for genuinely independent ETH/SOL or other-asset mechanisms; do not reuse the two low-timeframe baselines or ETH 30-minute Pine stack that failed pseudo-holdout.
7. Revisit $5,000 funding only after the v44 forward window is technically clean and economically positive. Capacity may remain below ten positions until independently qualified routes exist.

## Open decision boundary

No user input is required for the current research phase. The next irreversible decision is the later $5,000 capital increase; the evidence threshold for that decision is not met in this snapshot.
